title: Cohomology of an algebraic extension of a curve function field
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $C/k$ an integral
connected curve, and $L$ an algebraic extension
of its function field.
For every torsion etale sheaf
$M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}L$, its
cohomology vanishes
in degrees $q\geq2$.

proof.text:
By [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-filtered-union], [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit]
we may work with bounded-exponent torsion, and then with one
primary component. Use the exact field dictionary of
[lem-exc-field-discrete-modules]. The open subgroups of
$G_L$ correspond to finite separable extensions $E/L$.
We verify the hypothesis of [lem-sc-group-cd-one] for each one.

If $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, the field $E$ contains all
$\ell$-th roots of unity, so $\mu_\ell$ is a trivial
$\mathbf F_\ell$-module. The field Kummer calculation and
$H^1(E,\mathbf G_m)=\operatorname{Pic}(\operatorname{Spec}E)=0$
give the injection $H^2(E,\mu_\ell)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Br}(E)$
by [lem-sc-field-kummer-h2-brauer-injection]. The target vanishes
by [lem-sc-brauer-algebraic-function-field-zero].

If $\ell=\operatorname{char}k=p$, the polynomial argument for
$T^p-T-u$ gives the field Artin–Schreier exact sequence
[lem-sc-field-artin-schreier-sequence]. The two adjacent positive
cohomology groups of $\mathbf G_a$ on the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}E$
vanish by [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent], so $H^2(E,\mathbf F_p)=0$.
In both cases [lem-sc-group-cd-one] gives the assertion.
